newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta index ends lower as heavyweights lose.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta index ends lower as heavyweights lose.

text.p: The Jakarta stock index ended lower on Tuesday on locally-led profit-taking in Astra and limited foreign selling of some heavyweights, including Telkom and Indosat, brokers said.
The composite index was down 2.39 points, or 0.42 percent, at 568.59 points at the close after earlier touching a low of 567.55 points. Losers led gainers by 54 to 47, with 60 counters unchanged.
Brokers said the market was likely to be mixed on Wednesday, with some foreign players staying on the sidelines awaiting more positive news and local operators trading on a short-term basis.
Brokers said foreign money was waiting for upcoming initial public offerings in November despite the Monday overnight rise in the Dow and stronger regional markets.
"Most of them are awaiting the listing of Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI). We also heard the offering period will be brought forward to November 4 to 7 from November 6 to 11," a local broker said.
BNI, the largest state-owned bank, is currently conducting a roadshow in Asia, the United States and Europe ahead of the listing.
Bank BNI plans to float about 1.1 billion shares next month and is scheduled to announce the offer price on October 24. It will be the largest IPO on the Jakarta exchange this year.

Telecommunication firm Telkom and satellite operator Indosat were among the targets for limited foreign selling, brokers said. Telkom fell 1.39 percent to 3,550 rupiah from 3,600 on a volume of 812,500 shares, while Indosat fell 0.69 percent to 7,200 rupiah from 7,250 on 299,500 shares traded.
Car maker Astra traded unchanged at 3,925 rupiah with some 1.8 million shares changing hands. It fell to 3,800 rupiah in early trade on what brokers said was profit taking.
The volume of Astra stock was also boosted by cross-trading transactions which amounted 1.5 million shares, they said.
Glass and ceramic producer Mulia Industrindo topped the active list with a volume of 5.1 million shares, falling 25 rupiah to 2,275 on profit taking.

Shipping firm Rig Tender was also actively traded. It rose 75 rupiah to 1,475 on a turnover of 3.2 million shares. Brokers said this was due to continued market talk of a possible foreign takeover despite company denials.
